newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle crew found Mir in good shape.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle crew found Mir in good shape.

text.p: The crew of the space shuttle Atlantis found the Mir space station in good shape when they visited this week, despite recent mechanical problems on the ageing Russian outpost, NASA said on Thursday.

As Russian folk music played in the background, Atlantis pulled away from the 11-year-old Mir on Wednesday night, leaving behind British-born astronaut Michael Foale, who was beginning a four-month tour of duty in space.
"Mike's going to have a good stay up there," NASA Shuttle-Mir Programme Manager Frank Culbertson told a news conference on Thursday.

Atlantis left Foale behind in place of Jerry Linenger, a NASA astronaut from Michigan who had been aboard Mir since January. During his stay, Linenger and his Mir crewmates faced a serious fire in February, breakdowns in life support systems, cooling system leaks and a near miss with an unmanned cargo craft.

NASA had approved Foale's mission only after conditions aboard the station improved. On its trip to Mir, Atlantis also ferried a record 4,000 lbs (1,800 kg) of supplies and equipment, including a new device for generating breathing oxygen and repair gear to plug leaks in the station's cooling systems.

"The reports we got back from the crew and what we saw in the video and the pictures is that a lot of repair work has been done," Culbertson said. "There's still some more to be done, but in general they had come a long way."
Linenger, who spent 122 days aboard Mir, and his six shuttle crewmates were due to return to Earth this weekend.
Weather conditions looked favourable for a landing at the Kennedy Space Centre in Florida at 7:52 a.m. EDT (1152 GMT) on Saturday, mission operations director Lee Briscoe said.
Atlantis is to return to Mir in September to collect Foale and drop off another NASA astronaut.
